pluss::series::undefined¶

Back to Series Factory API Reference

Signature¶

Series pluss::series::undefined()

What It Builds¶

undefined() creates an explicit absence sentinel. It does not allocate numeric storage, choose a dtype, or represent an empty shape. Its only purpose is to let an API carry “no Series was supplied” while keeping that state inside the Series type.

The same state is available through public default construction:

pluss::Series pending{};

Neither spelling creates numeric data. Use {} as the concise form for local placeholders and fields that will be assigned later. Use pluss::series::undefined() when naming the absence is clearer, especially in function arguments, conditional expressions, and returned sentinel values. Defined values still come from public factories.

Do not substitute an empty series such as pluss::series::empty({0}, ...). That object is defined, has dtype and shape metadata, and participates in ordinary operations. An undefined series has no payload at all.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series

An undefined handle for optional state. defined() returns false for the result.

Where It Belongs¶

Use the sentinel at boundaries where absence is part of the contract:

  • an optional bias, mask, initial state, or cached result

  • a field that will be assigned by a later initialization phase

  • a branch whose caller already checks defined() before numerical use

Prefer std::optional<Series> when the surrounding API is naturally expressed as an optional C++ value. pluss::series::undefined() is most useful in tensor-shaped interfaces where an undefined handle is already the established absence protocol and where keeping one concrete parameter type simplifies dispatch.

The sentinel is not a delayed allocation. Numerical methods reject it; call a value factory such as make, zeros, or empty before doing arithmetic.

Examples¶

Example 1. The factory creates an explicit undefined state.

const auto absent = pluss::series::undefined();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "defined=" << absent.defined() << "\n";

Output¶

defined=false

Example 2. An optional parameter can carry either a normal factory result or the named sentinel while keeping both branches the same type.

const bool supply_bias = false;
const auto bias = supply_bias
    ? pluss::series::zeros({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64)
    : pluss::series::undefined();

std::cout << std::boolalpha << "bias_defined=" << bias.defined() << "\n";

Output¶

bias_defined=false

The same variable can later receive a factory-built Series through ordinary copy or move assignment.

Example 3. Default construction is the compact spelling when several fields begin in the undefined state.

pluss::Series lb{}, ub{}, scaler{}, pen_val{};

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << lb.defined() << " "
          << ub.defined() << " "
          << scaler.defined() << " "
          << pen_val.defined() << "\n";

Output¶

false false false false

Example 4. Undefined is not a numeric value. Arithmetic fails before a result is produced.

const auto absent = pluss::series::undefined();

try {
  (void)absent.add(1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  const std::string message = e.what();
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

SeriesBase: undefined

Failure Modes¶

  • Arithmetic, indexing, shape queries that require storage, and device transfer reject an undefined receiver.

  • undefined() does not accept a dtype, platform, or shape because those properties belong to defined storage.

  • Do not print or serialize the sentinel as if it were data. Test defined() and encode absence explicitly at the surrounding protocol boundary.

Performance And Ownership¶

Default construction and pluss::series::undefined() perform no data allocation or element copy. The check performed by defined() is constant time. Replacing either form by assignment follows normal intrusive-handle ownership rules for the newly assigned Series.

Summary¶

Use Series{} for a concise undefined placeholder or pluss::series::undefined() to state absence explicitly. Use a value factory for every numeric object, including zero-element series.

See Also¶

  • pluss::series::empty: allocate defined, uninitialized storage.

  • pluss::series::zeros: allocate a defined zero-filled value.

  • pluss::series::make: construct defined data from host values.
